expected.description: Hardcoded API key / secret in source

matched.actual_description: The variable 'STRIPE_API_KEY' is set to a hardcoded string. Even though the current value is '<redacted>', the pattern of hardcoding secrets in source code violates CWE-798. If a real key were inserted, it would be exposed in version control and leak. Secrets must be loaded from environment variables or a secret manager.

expected.description: Insecure MD5 hash used for password storage

matched.actual_description: The function hash_user_password uses hashlib.md5() to hash passwords. MD5 is cryptographically broken, prone to collision attacks, and far too fast for password hashing. This violates CWE-327 and exposes user credentials to cracking.

expected.description: Path traversal via unsanitized filename in os.path.join

matched.actual_description: The function read_user_file concatenates unsanitized user input into a file path using os.path.join. An attacker can supply sequences like '../../../etc/passwd' to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files on the system (CWE-22).

expected.description: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on untrusted data

matched.actual_description: The function load_session_data deserializes user-supplied data using pickle.loads. The pickle module is inherently unsafe for untrusted data and allows arbitrary code execution, leading to remote code execution (CWE-502).

expected.description: OS command injection via os.system with unsanitized input

matched.actual_description: The ping_host function constructs a shell command string with unsanitized user input and executes it via os.system. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary commands (e.g., '8.8.8.8; cat /etc/passwd') (CWE-78).

expected.description: Command injection via subprocess.run with shell=True

matched.actual_title: OS Command Injection via subprocess with shell=True
matched.actual_description: Even after attempting a fix, the ping_host function calls subprocess.run with shell=True and unsanitized user input, which is equally vulnerable to command injection (CWE-78). The shell=True parameter interprets the string as a shell command, allowing injection.

expected.description: SSRF: unvalidated user-supplied avatar_url passed to requests.get

matched.actual_title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Local File Disclosure via user-controlled avatar URL
matched.actual_description: The function fetch_avatar takes an avatar_url from request.json and directly passes it to requests.get without any validation of the URL scheme or destination. An attacker can supply a URL pointing to internal services (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) or use file:// scheme to read local files, leading to sensitive data exposure or further exploitation.

expected.description: SSRF via unvalidated avatar_url in fetch_avatar

matched.actual_title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in avatar fetching
matched.actual_description: The fetch_avatar function sends a GET request to a user-controlled avatar_url without any validation or restrictions. An attacker can supply internal URLs or cloud metadata endpoints to scan networks or exfiltrate sensitive data.

expected.description: IDOR: get_invoice does not verify authenticated_user_id owns the invoice

matched.actual_title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in invoice retrieval
matched.actual_description: get_invoice retrieves an invoice by its ID without checking that it belongs to the authenticated user (authenticated_user_id is never compared to the invoice's user_id). Any authenticated user can access arbitrary invoices, leading to unauthorized disclosure of billing data.
A hardcoded JWT secret key is used in verify_token. This exposes the secret to anyone with access to the source code and allows attackers to forge valid tokens if the key becomes known.

expected.description: JWT algorithm confusion: 'none' algorithm accepted allows signature bypass

matched.actual_title: JWT algorithm confusion: acceptance of 'none' algorithm
matched.actual_description: The jwt.decode call allows the 'none' algorithm, enabling attackers to craft tokens with empty signatures that completely bypass authentication.
